alt: A finished first relief carving of a wolf held up proudly in two hands in a home workshop
A blank cherry board clamped flat on a CNC spoilboard with four low clamps at the corners, ready to carve
The wolf design half way through the roughing pass, the right half still uncut blank and the left half stepped terraces
The back of the finished panel with a keyhole slot, felt bumpers and the maker's initials burned in
A plain one inch cherry board, 300 by 350 mm, standing on edge on the workbench with a steel rule beside it
The three cutters for a first relief carving: a quarter inch flat end mill, a 1/16 inch tapered ball nose and a 1/32 inch tapered ball nose
A small test tile with the wolf's head carved on a cherry offcut, held beside the blank board
The wolf relief mid semi-finish on the machine, a tapered ball nose smoothing the roughed terraces into the finished surface
A soft brass brush lifting the machining fuzz off the raw wolf carving, the brushed half visibly cleaner
Dark glaze being wiped back off the wolf carving with a rag, the wiped half showing the finished contrast
Drawn plan of the three toolpaths seen from above: roughing and semi-finish inside the model outline, the fine pass inside a boundary around the wolf
The finished first relief carving on the workbench with the three cutters, the test tile and a keyhole hanger laid out in front of it
